A.explanation: Far too small for any metal at room temperature. Copper resistivity is about $1.7 \times 10^{-8}$ $\Omega \text{m}$, five orders larger.

B.explanation: Copper is an excellent conductor with resistivity about $1.7 \times 10^{-8}$ $\Omega \text{m}$, so order $10^{-8}$ $\Omega \text{m}$.

walkthrough: Identify what is asked: the material property resistivity $\rho$ of copper, defined by $R = \rho L / A$, measured in $\Omega \text{m}$.
Recall copper is chosen for wires because it is an excellent conductor, so its $\rho$ must be very small, much smaller than semiconductors and insulators.
Recall the learned typical value: $\rho$ for copper is about $1.7 \times 10^{-8}$ $\Omega \text{m}$ at room temperature.
Check orders: $10^{-13}$ $\Omega \text{m}$ is impossibly low, $10^{-3}$ $\Omega \text{m}$ fits a semiconductor, and $10^{2}$ $\Omega \text{m}$ fits an insulator.
Therefore the $10^{-8}$ $\Omega \text{m}$ order matches copper. This is option B.
